questions.text: Is your ISMS scope defined and approved — covering locations, systems, services, and explicit exclusions?
Has top management assigned roles, committed resources, and stayed visibly engaged in security governance?
Is a risk assessment methodology defined and applied consistently, with criteria, scoring, and risk appetite documented?
Is a live risk register maintained, with named owners, treatment plans, due dates, and a review cadence?
Is your Statement of Applicability complete — included/excluded controls, justifications, status, owner, and evidence pointers?
Is access control governed — joiner/mover/leaver process, role-based access, MFA, and privileged access controls?
Is centralised security logging and alerting in place for identity, endpoints, cloud, and critical applications?
Is your incident response plan documented, tested, and improved after exercises or real incidents?
Are internal ISMS audits performed against a plan, with findings tracked to verified closure?
Are management reviews held at planned intervals, covering risks, incidents, KPIs, audit results, and improvements?
